sentence: This project designs and tests tailored strategies to address HIV and drug use among men who have sex with men engaged in high-risk sex.
This project uses the worm C. elegans to study how small packages called extracellular vesicles work in nerve cells of a living animal.
This project looks for blood markers of meal timing and studies how meal timing relates to cancers of the breast, colon and rectum, and endometrium.
This project studies how extended high-frequency hearing loss affects speech understanding in noisy places and awareness of the space around a person.
This project studies imaging and molecular data to find target genes in pediatric low-grade glioma, then tests them in fly models and tumor organoids.
This project builds engineered botulinum toxins for treating bladder disorders and an engineered antibody that can neutralize and clear the toxins.
This project uses machine learning on genes, cell features and images of atherosclerotic plaques to find what makes lesions vulnerable.
This project studies how cholesterol controls the making and movement of phosphatidylserine in cells, using structural, biochemical and cell biological methods.
This project studies how proteins on the cell surface sense and respond to force, which matters in diseases like cancer and heart disease.
This project builds brain organoids with tiny built-in electronics and tests whether transplanting them can restore motor function after chronic stroke.
This project studies how proteins control the length of muscle thin filaments and how this is linked to human muscle and heart diseases.
This project tries to ease medical translation by having healthcare professionals edit machine translations while doing learning exercises.
This project tries to find out how low oxygen changes the movement and function of macrophages in pancreatic cancer.
This project tests whether a radiotracer for a cell transporter can show how sensitive cancers are to ferroptosis, a form of regulated cell death.
This project studies how the Orsay virus enters cells in the intestine of C. elegans through a receptor protein.
This project studies how an immune regulator acts on microglia and macrophages as gliomas, which are brain tumors, progress.
This project makes small molecule drugs that activate the immune system against cancer and checks them for possible toxicity.
This project studies how HIV hides and restarts in microglia and macrophages of the central nervous system when cocaine is present.
This project collects blood samples and clinical information from patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease to find markers of its different features.
This project builds biomarkers using mass spectrometry to measure metal-protein interactions and study their role in aging and neurodegenerative disease.
